To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cellulose oxygen isotope record from Bristlecones contains a large shift in mean values that correlates with a major climate shift across northern hemisphere, and that this record contains a bidecadally oscillating signal that is not well correlated with drought variability in the region.

the cellulose δ 18O record from the Bristlecone pine tree in White Mountain, California, shows two distinctive characteristics: (1) a bidecadally oscillating signal with peak excursions up to 4‰ and (2) a dramatic 9 ‰ shift in mean δ 18O values in mid-19th century.

the cellulose δ 18OVSMOW of the long-lived BCP from the White Mountains shows two distinctive features: (1) a bidecadally varying pattern of isotopic variability that peaked at 4‰ during the 20 th century and (2) a dramatic 9 ‰ shift in the isotopic composition in the mid- 19 th century that is correlated with the major shift in climate across the northern hemisphere.
